Title: SK hynix's first PCIe 5.0 SSD is finally available in the U.S., sports impressive performance and pricing — Platinum P51 flaunts speeds up to 14,700 MB/s | Tom's Hardware
URL: https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/ssds/sk-hynixs-first-consumer-pcie-5-0-ssd-is-finally-available-in-the-u-s-market-platinum-p51-flaunts-speeds-up-to-14-700-mb-s
Published: 2025-07-02T16:52:34.000Z
Author: Zhiye Liu
Highlights:
The Platinum P51, the successor to the highly acclaimed Platinum P41, has finally been introduced to the United States market. Initially unveiled in March of the previous year and subsequently launched exclusively in South Korea in December, the Platinum P51 traveled a long distance to reach this hemisphere, but they're now here and SK hynix has priced the Platinum P51 very competitively: The 1TB version is available for $169.99, and the 2TB sports a $269.99 price tag to contend with the best SSDs on the market.

The Platinum P51 employs SK hynix's in-house PCIe 5.0 SSD controller. In this instance, the manufacturer has implemented the Alistar ACNT093 controller, characterized by an eight-channel architecture and capable of supporting transfer rates up to 2,400 MT/s. Information regarding the ACNT093 is sparse. The SSD controller utilizes Arm's 32-bit Cortex-R8 processor and is believed to be fabricated on a 10nm process node, which TSMC likely supplies.

SK hynix combines the ACNT093 controller with the company's 238-layer 3D V8 TLC NAND. It represents a significant upgrade from the 176-layer NAND used in the previous Platinum P41. As with its predecessor, the Platinum P51 also includes LPDDR4 DRAM, though its capacity has not been disclosed. SK hynix hasn't yet uploaded a product page for the Platinum P51.

## SK hynix Platinum P51 Specifications

| Model | Capacity | Sequential Read (MB/s) | Sequential Write (MB/s) | Random Read (IOPS) | Random Write (IOPS) | Endurance (TBW) | MSRP |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SKH-P51-2TB | 2TB | 14,700 | 13,400 | 2,300,000 | 2,400,000 | 1,200 | $269.99 |
| SKH-P51-1TB | 1TB | 14,700 | 12,900 | 2,300,000 | 2,400,000 | 600 | $169.99 |

The Platinum P51 M.2 2280 SSD is exclusively available in two capacities: 1TB and 2TB. It appears that SK hynix will not sell a 500GB variant, a capacity that was available with the Platinum P41 or the Gold P31 before it. According to the specifications sheet, the Platinum P51 achieves sequential read speeds of up to 14,700 MB/s. The sequential write performance, however, varies depending on the capacity. The 2TB model tops out at 13,400 MB/s while the 1TB model has 4% lower sequential write performance.

On the other hand, random performance is equal between the two drives. Both can reach random read and write speeds up to 2,300,000 IOPS and 2,400,000 IOPS, respectively. The Platinum P51's performance figures place the drive alongside the Sandisk WD Black SN8100, Samsung 9100 Pro, or Crucial T705.

Title: SK hynix Platinum P51 Gen5 2TB SSD Review - SK hynix Strikes Gold With Their Alistar Gen5 SSD Controller | The SSD Review
URL: https://www.thessdreview.com/our-reviews/nvme/sk-hynix-platinum-p51-gen5-2tb-ssd-review/
Published: 2025-08-28T12:04:38.000Z
Author: Les Tokar
Highlights:
The SK hynix Platinum P51 is a PCIe 5.0 (Gen5) 4-channel (x4) SSD of the 2280 form factor (22mm wide x 80mm long) which is of the NVMe 2.0 SSD operating protocol. It is available in one and two terabyte capacities and performance specifications speak to 14700MB/s read and 13400MB/s write data throughput.

Perhaps our greatest interest in this SSD lies in the fact that its brand new SSD controller is proprietary to SK hynix which is not the current norm, and further, this controller is the SK hynix Alistar Gen5 8-channel NVMe SSD controller. To the left of this is a SK hynix DRAM buffer chip.

This is a ‘single-sided’ SSD with two 1TB NAND flash memory packages on the PCB which are SK hynix 238-layer 3D TLC NAND flash memory.

This SSD is a ‘thoroughbred’ storage device. It has a typical 10 watt active power usage which is a bit high in consideration of where we see other SSDs bringing that power rating down to sub 8 watts as of late.

Checking Amazon, we can find the Platinum P51 for $154.99 (1TB) and $229.99 (2TB) which is significantly lower than the original MSRP of $199.99/$319.99. This SSD comes with a standard 5-year limited warranty and speaks to 600TBW endurance per 1TB of capacity.

Title: SK hynix Platinum P51 2TB PCIe Gen 5 NVMe SSD Review - SK hynix Platinum P51 2TB PCIe Gen 5 NVMe SSD Review
URL: https://www.neoseeker.com/Articles/Hardware/Reviews/sk-hynix-platinum-p51-2tb/
Published: 2026-10-15T09:53:26.000Z
Author: Mark Watkins
Highlights:
The Platinum P51 combines SK hynix's in-house Alistar Gen5 controller with 238-layer 3D TLC NAND and onboard LPDDR4 DRAM. Our 2TB review sample carries official sequential performance ratings of up to 14,700 MB/s read and 13,400 MB/s write, along with random performance ratings of up to 2.3 million read IOPS and 2.4 million write IOPS. Endurance is rated at 1,200 TBW for the 2TB model and the drive is backed by a five-year warranty.

...

Inside, the Platinum P51 is housed in a molded protective tray alongside the user documentation and warranty information. The drive itself uses the standard M.2 2280 form factor and is a single-sided design, improving compatibility with desktops and notebooks where component clearance may be limited.

The P51 does not include a large factory heatsink, instead using a thin label across the primary components. Underneath, the 2TB model combines SK hynix's in-house Alistar ACNT093 eight-channel PCIe 5.0 controller with 238-layer TLC NAND and LPDDR4 DRAM. This vertically integrated design gives SK hynix control over the controller, flash, firmware, and memory rather than relying on a common third-party Gen5 controller platform.

 

### SK hynix Platinum P51 2TB PCIe Gen 5 NVMe SSD Features

| Capacity | 1TB / 2TB |
| --- | --- |
| Form Factor | M.2 2280 |
| Interface | PCIe 5.0 x4 |
| NVMe Standard | NVMe 2.0 |
| Controller | SK hynix Alistar Gen5 |
| NAND Flash | SK hynix 238-Layer 3D TLC NAND |
| DRAM Cache | LPDDR4 |
| Sequential Read | Up to 14,700 MB/s |
| Sequential Write | Up to 12,900 MB/s (1TB) / 13,400 MB/s (2TB) |
| Random Read | Up to 2,300,000 IOPS |
| Random Write | Up to 2,400,000 IOPS |
| Endurance | 600 TBW (1TB) / 1,200 TBW (2TB) |
| Warranty | 5-Year Limited Warranty |

...

CrystalDiskInfo confirms that the Platinum P51 negotiated a full PCIe 5.0 x4 connection and operated using the NVMe 2.0 standard. Our sample was running firmware 61060A50 and reported 100% health following testing.

 

 

CrystalDiskMark measured sequential performance of 13,827.67 MB/s read and 12,932.80 MB/s write. That places our sample within roughly 6% of SK hynix's official 14,700 MB/s read rating and within approximately 4% of its 13,400 MB/s write specification. Sequential Q1T1 performance remained impressive at 9,960.29 MB/s read and 10,297.73 MB/s write.

...

SK hynix's much higher advertised random IOPS figures are measured under different queue-depth and workload conditions, so they should not be directly compared with

...

The SK hynix Platinum P51 2TB delivers exactly the sort of performance expected from a flagship PCIe 5.0 SSD. Our sample reached 13.83 GB/s sequential reads and 12.93 GB/s sequential writes in CrystalDiskMark, landing close to SK hynix's already ambitious specifications while also delivering excellent sustained write behavior in AIDA64.

The PCIe 4.0 comparison is arguably just as interesting. Limited to Gen4, the P51 still reached almost 6.9 GB/s in both directions and retained essentially the same random 4K performance. Moving to PCIe 5.0 therefore provides an enormous advantage for bandwidth-heavy sequential workloads, but users should not expect everyday low-queue random access to suddenly double along with the interface bandwidth.

SK hynix's vertically integrated design is another strength. The P51 combines an in-house controller, 238-layer TLC NAND, dedicated LPDDR4 DRAM, a single-sided M.2 2280 layout, 1,200TBW endurance rating, and five-year warranty. It also avoids the sustained-write collapse seen on some more heavily cache-dependent consumer SSDs, maintaining multi-gigabyte-per-second throughput even after its highest-speed operating region has been exhausted.

Title: SK hynix Platinum P51 Review: Balanced Performance for Demanding Workloads
URL: https://www.storagereview.com/review/sk-hynix-platinum-p51-review-balanced-performance-for-demanding-workloads
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
SK hynix positions the Platinum P51 as an ideal solution for content creators, developers, and users with demanding workloads. At its core is SK hynix’s proprietary Gen5 controller, paired with 238-layer 3D TLC NAND (ACNT093), engineered to prioritize data integrity, high storage density, and long-term endurance. The 238-layer NAND structure helps increase storage capacity without compromising reliability, while the controller is designed to deliver stable performance under heavy loads.

With quoted sequential speeds of up to 14,700MB/s read and 13,400MB/s write, the Platinum P51 holds its own among the latest Gen5 consumer SSDs. Moreover, while some high-end SSDs require aggressive cooling to maintain consistent speeds, SK hynix’s new SSD is engineered with a power draw of just 10W, making it one of the more efficient options currently available. This emphasis on thermal performance means the drive is less likely to throttle under sustained tasks, potentially making it a better fit for compact systems or creative workstations that require uninterrupted operation. SK hynix claims this combination results in consistent performance even during prolonged high-output scenarios. As always, we’ll verify how well this all translates into real-world performance (in areas like random read IOPS, game loading, and content streaming) with our benchmarking below. Still, the drive presents itself as a solid choice for users building a new system or upgrading to a Gen5 platform.

As of this review, the SK hynix Platinum P51 is priced at $169.99 for the 1TB model and $269.99 for the 2TB version at Amazon (affiliate link). That places it slightly above the entry-level Gen5 SSD tier, but still well below some premium options in its class, which means SK hynix is targeting users who want high-end specs without overcommitting on cost.

Backed by a 5-year warranty and 2-million-hour MTBF rating, we will be looking at the 2TB model for this review.
